title: Sankarabharanam
tropes: Revered Carnatic classical singer Sankara Sastry faces social boycott in a traditional town/village
Courtesan's daughter Tulasi worships classical music and finds shelter under his roof
Pure platonic guru-shishya devotion tested by societal gossip and western pop trends
National Film Award-winning cultural milestone of vintage Telugu cinema
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Timeless classical songs like 'Omkara Nadhanu' and 'Brochevarevarura'
hint: A 1980 National Award musical classic where Carnatic ragas triumph over prejudice.
eraTrivia: Released in February 1980 to empty theatres initially before word-of-mouth turned it into a historic silver-jubilee phenomenon across South India

Won 4 National Film Awards including Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment, Best Music Direction (K.V. Mahadevan), Best Male Playback Singer (S.P.B.), and Best Female Playback Singer (Vani Jairam)
Winner of the Prix du Public (Audience Prize) at the Besancon Film Festival in France in 1981
Featured in CNN-IBN's list of 100 Greatest Indian Films of All Time
Sparked a nationwide revival of interest in Carnatic classical music among 1980s youth
Does not feature Brahmanandam (released before his film debut)
iconicMoments: Soul-stirring dawn Carnatic concert sequences photographed by Balu Mahendra
Graceful classical Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dance frames in rain and temple courtyards
An unforgettable concert climax where a young disciple continues his guru's unbroken raga

pressHints.headline: Won the Audience Prize at France's Besançon Film Festival
pressHints.body: Rarely for an Indian regional film of its era, it captivated European festival crowds in 1981 and later landed on CNN-IBN's 100 Greatest Indian Films of All Time.

pressHints.headline: Started Quietly in Feb 1980, Then Sparked a Cultural Wave
pressHints.body: Distributors initially worried it had no commercial stars—until glowing word-of-mouth turned empty matinees into packed silver-jubilee runs across Andhra and Tamil Nadu.

pressHints.headline: 4 National Film Awards Including Both Playback Singers
pressHints.body: S.P. Balasubrahmanyam, Vani Jairam, and composer K.V. Mahadevan all took home National Film Awards alongside Best Popular Film.

pressHints.headline: Kalatapasvi K. Viswanath + Balu Mahendra + Veturi
pressHints.body: Produced by Edida Nageswara Rao's Poornodaya banner, pairing K. Viswanath's direction with Veturi's timeless Telugu lyrics and Balu Mahendra's cinematography.

pressHints.headline: Carnatic Tambura, Classical Ragas & 'Omkara Nadhanu'
pressHints.body: Remembered as Telugu cinema's supreme classical musical classic starring J.V. Somayajulu and Manju Bhargavi, reviving Carnatic music for an entire generation.

title: Athadu
tropes: Professional sniper and hitman Nandu framed for a politician's assassination
Escapes on a train and assumes the identity of a dead man named Pardhu
Warm joint family in a rural village backdrop (Basarlapudi) welcomes him as their long-lost grandson
Sharp CBI officer Anjaneya Prasad (Prakash Raj) investigates the murder
Features Brahmanandam as Kittu, the hilarious relative in the village house
Iconic punch dialogues, train chase, and family wedding action climax
iconicProp: High-powered sniper rifle & Pardhu's silver wristwatch
hint: A hitman jumps off a train and accidentally becomes the favorite grandson of a lively village family.
eraTrivia: Released August 10, 2005 after nearly three years in production, including a rare song shoot in Poland
Won 3 Nandi Awards (Best Actor, Best Dialogue Writer, Best Special Effects) and Filmfare Best Director
Holds legendary cult status with 1,500+ re-telecasts on Star Maa TV
Remade in Hindi as 'Ek: The Power of One' (2009) and Bengali as 'Wanted' (2010)
First feature collaboration between Mahesh Babu and Trivikram Srinivas
iconicMoments: Sleek slow-motion rain-drenched action sequence choreographed by Peter Hein
Deadpan wedding-house comedy lines with Sunil and Brahmanandam
Timeless 'pappu' dinner-table sarcasm that became an evergreen Telugu meme

pressHints.headline: Three Years in Production & A Rare Song Shoot in Poland
pressHints.body: Backed by veteran actor Murali Mohan's Jayabheri Arts banner, it faced long schedule delays and became one of the rare mid-2000s Telugu films to shoot a song in Poland.

pressHints.headline: 3 Nandi Awards, Overseas Record & A 2009 Hindi Remake
pressHints.body: Released in August 2005, it set US box-office milestones, won 3 Nandi Awards (including Best Dialogue Writer), and was later remade in Hindi and Bengali.

pressHints.headline: K.V. Guhan + Sreekar Prasad + Peter Hein + Mani Sharma
pressHints.body: Celebrated for its Hollywood-sleek framing, razor-sharp editing, and atmospheric rain-drenched action set pieces alongside a powerhouse ensemble cast.

pressHints.headline: First Collaboration of Mahesh Babu & Trivikram Srinivas
pressHints.body: Marked the very first feature film teaming up Superstar Mahesh Babu and writer-director Trivikram Srinivas, co-starring Trisha, Prakash Raj, Sonu Sood, and Brahmanandam.

pressHints.headline: 1,500+ Star Maa TV Telecasts & Evergreen 'Pappu' Memes
pressHints.body: Widely joked as the unofficial national anthem of Telugu Sunday afternoons on Star Maa TV—famous for its deadpan family-wedding wit and sniper precision.

title: Pokiri
tropes: Ruthless local gangster Pandu secretly works as undercover IPS officer Krishna Manohar
Mumbai mafia don Ali Bhai (Prakash Raj) runs a violent syndicate in Hyderabad
Romance with aerobics instructor Shruti stalked by a corrupt cop
Features Brahmanandam as Brahmi, a hilarious software engineer neighbor
Massive climax identity plot twist with 'Okkasari commit ayithe naa maata nene vinanu'
Urban gang war, shootouts, and mass item songs
iconicProp: IPS Officer ID badge & Pandu's yellow checkered shirt
hint: Once he commits, he doesn't even listen to himself—and his biggest secret drops in the climax.
eraTrivia: Released April 28, 2006 and became an all-time Telugu industry hit—holding the top box-office record for over 3 years
Screened at the 7th IIFA Awards Film Festival in Dubai in 2006
Remade in Tamil (Vijay's 'Pokkiri'), Hindi (Salman Khan's 'Wanted'), and Kannada ('Porki')—launching massive comebacks in multiple industries
Won 2 Nandi Awards and 2 Filmfare Awards South including Best Film and Best Director
Produced jointly by Puri Jagannadh (Vaishno Academy) and Manjula Ghattamaneni (Indira Productions)
iconicMoments: The legendary elevator/train-yard swagger and 'Okkasari commit ayithe...' punchline
Brahmanandam's hilarious software engineer frustration track and Ali's 'Beggars Association' comedy
Chartbuster 2006 mass anthem 'Ippatikinka Naa Vayasu' and 'Dole Dole'

pressHints.headline: Remade in 3 Languages & Ignited Box-Office Comebacks Across India
pressHints.body: After becoming a Telugu juggernaut in 2006, it was remade in Tamil, Hindi, and Kannada—with its Hindi remake reviving a Bollywood superstar's mass-action career in 2009.

pressHints.headline: Held the All-Time Telugu Box-Office Crown for Over 3 Years
pressHints.body: Released in late April 2006 and ran for 175+ days across scores of centres—even earning a special screening at the IIFA Film Festival in Dubai.

pressHints.headline: Software Engineer Brahmi, Beggars Association & 'Ippatikinka'
pressHints.body: Balanced gritty urban crime drama with unforgettable comedy tracks by Brahmanandam, Ali, and Venu Madhav—plus a Mani Sharma mass soundtrack that dominated 2006.

pressHints.headline: Puri Jagannadh + Mahesh Babu + Ileana + Prakash Raj
pressHints.body: Directed by Puri Jagannadh and starring Mahesh Babu alongside Ileana D'Cruz, with Prakash Raj and Ashish Vidyarthi playing ruthless antagonists.

pressHints.headline: 'Okkasari Commit Ayithe Naa Maata Nene Vinanu!'
pressHints.body: Famous for one of Telugu cinema's greatest climax reveals and a yellow checkered-shirt swagger that redefined mass heroes forever.

title: Bommarillu
tropes: Overprotective father (Prakash Raj) controls every tiny decision in his son Siddhu's life
Bubbly, quirky heroine Hasini ('Ha-Ha-Hasini!') transforms Siddhu's rigid world
Heroine stays at the hero's family home for seven days to win over his dad
Features Brahmanandam in a memorable comic cameo as a loan recovery officer
Iconic emotional climax outburst: 'Motham meere chesaru!'
Feel-good urban family romance with chartbuster songs like 'Appudo Ippudo'
iconicProp: Two-scoop ice cream cone & an orange shirt chosen by dad
hint: Every shirt, career, and fiancée was picked by his father—until 'Ha-Ha-Hasini' walked in.
eraTrivia: Released August 9, 2006 as Bhaskar's directorial debut and became a youth-and-family blockbuster under Dil Raju's banner
Swept 7 Nandi Awards (including Best Feature Film, Best Debut Director, Best Supporting Actor for Prakash Raj, Best Special Jury for Genelia) and 4 Filmfare Awards South
Remade across India in Tamil ('Santosh Subramaniam'), Hindi ('It's My Life'), Bengali, Odia, and Marathi
Siddharth sang the smash-hit youth anthem 'Appudo Ippudo' himself for DSP's soundtrack
The director became permanently nicknamed after this film's title in Tollywood
iconicMoments: The legendary 'Ha-Ha-Hasini!' introduction and quirky ice-cream parlor banter
An unforgettable tear-jerking father-son dining-room confrontation ('Motham meere chesaru!')
Brahmanandam's brief but riotous loan-recovery cameo and Sunil's kitchen comedy

pressHints.headline: A Debut Film So Huge It Permanently Renamed Its Director
pressHints.body: Produced by Dil Raju in 2006, this debut directorial swept 7 Nandi Awards and earned its director a permanent prefix nickname across the Telugu industry.

pressHints.headline: Remade in Tamil ('Santosh Subramaniam'), Hindi, Bengali & Odia
pressHints.body: Its relatable generational conflict struck such a deep chord in August 2006 that filmmakers across five Indian languages rushed to remake it.

pressHints.headline: The Lead Hero Sang DSP's Hit Track 'Appudo Ippudo' Himself
pressHints.body: Devi Sri Prasad delivered an all-time youth album—with the hero stepping into the recording booth himself and Abburi Ravi penning razor-sharp family dialogues.

pressHints.headline: Siddharth + Genelia + Prakash Raj + Jayasudha + Sunil
pressHints.body: Prakash Raj won both the Nandi and Filmfare trophies for his unforgettable overprotective father role opposite Siddharth and a bubbly Genelia D'Souza.

pressHints.headline: 'Ha-Ha-Hasini!', Orange Shirts & 'Motham Meere Chesaru!'
pressHints.body: Immortalized by an eccentric ice-cream-loving heroine and the most quoted father-son emotional climax monologue in modern Telugu cinema.

title: Jalsa
tropes: Opened and narrated throughout by Mahesh Babu's witty voiceover
Carefree college student Sanjay Sahu hides a tragic past as a former Naxalite
Factionist villain Damodar Reddy (Mukesh Rishi) has a fierce rural faction backdrop
Features Brahmanandam in an iconic hilarious track as Pranav
Romance involving two sisters Indu and Bhagyamati with comedy college fights
Superhit soundtrack including 'My Heart Is Beating' and 'Gallo Thelinattunde'
iconicProp: Red Naxalite bandana & college hostel guitar
hint: Narrated by Mahesh Babu, this carefree college hero hides a fiery past—and tortures Pranav.
eraTrivia: Released April 2, 2008 as the first collaboration between Pawan Kalyan and Trivikram Srinivas, scoring the highest Telugu opening of 2008
Famously opened and narrated throughout by Superstar Mahesh Babu's witty voiceover—a massive fan surprise in theatres
Produced by Allu Aravind under Geetha Arts with music by Devi Sri Prasad
Its 2008 audio launch and soundtrack ('My Heart Is Beating', 'Gallo Thelinattunde', 'Jennifer Lopez', 'You & I') broke audio sales records
Later got a massive 4K theatrical re-release celebration in 2022
iconicMoments: Brahmanandam's legendary 'Pranav' comedy sequence—one of the most quoted comedy tracks in Telugu cinema
Mahesh Babu's cheeky narration introducing the protagonist's carefree philosophy
Sharp Trivikram wit balancing hostel laughs with an intense flashback

pressHints.headline: A Rival Superstar Provided the Witty Voiceover Narration
pressHints.body: When it released in April 2008, theatres erupted at the very start when fans recognized another top Telugu superstar delivering the sarcastic narration!

pressHints.headline: Highest Opening of 2008 & A Massive 4K Re-Release Craze
pressHints.body: Backed by Allu Aravind's Geetha Arts, it smashed opening-day records in 2008 and became one of the pioneers of Tollywood's 4K fan re-release wave in 2022.

pressHints.headline: DSP's 'My Heart Is Beating' & 'Gallo Thelinattunde' Mania
pressHints.body: Devi Sri Prasad's energetic youth soundtrack ruled every college campus in 2008, aided by Rasool Ellore's visuals and Sreekar Prasad's snappy cuts.

pressHints.headline: First Team-Up of Power Star Pawan Kalyan & Trivikram
pressHints.body: Paired Pawan Kalyan with director Trivikram Srinivas for the very first time, co-starring Ileana D'Cruz, Parvati Melton, Prakash Raj, and Mukesh Rishi.

pressHints.headline: Brahmanandam's Legendary 'Pranav!' Comedy Track
pressHints.body: Forever immortalized on meme pages for Brahmanandam getting hilariously terrorized as Pranav—plus 'Yuddham lo gelavadam ante...'

title: Magadheera
tropes: 400-year reincarnation love story spanning 1609 Udaigarh kingdom and modern Hyderabad
Royal warrior Kala Bhairava fights 100 soldiers alone on a bridge for Princess Mitravinda
Modern street bike racer Harsha gets electric flashbacks whenever he touches Indu
Features Brahmanandam in a comic cameo as Indu's neighbor
Srihari plays Sher Khan who transforms from rival to ally across lifetimes
Helicopter climax battle and epic period fantasy visuals
hint: One touch sparks 400 years of memories—and one warrior takes on 100 soldiers.
eraTrivia: Released July 31, 2009 and shattered Telugu box-office records, famously running 1,000 consecutive days in Kurnool
Made on Tollywood's highest budget (~40 crore) at the time for just the lead hero's second film
Won 2 National Film Awards (Best Choreography & Best Special Effects) and 9 Nandi Awards
Featured a surprise Megastar Chiranjeevi cameo in the remixed 'Bangaru Kodipetta' song
Shot across Rann of Kutch, Dholavira, Badami, and grand Ramoji Film City sets
iconicMoments: Chariot-and-horseback chase across arid salt flats and fort walls
Roaring 'Okkokkanni kaadu Sher Khan, vanda mandini okesaari pampu!' elevation dialogue
Electric touch flashbacks and aerial helicopter climax

pressHints.headline: Famously Ran 1,000 Consecutive Days in Kurnool
pressHints.body: After releasing in late July 2009, this juggernaut shattered the all-time Telugu industry record and set a jaw-dropping 1,000-day theatrical run milestone.

pressHints.headline: 2 National Film Awards & 9 Nandi Trophies
pressHints.body: Won National Awards for Best Choreography and Best Special Effects—shot across the Rann of Kutch, Dholavira, and Badami by K.K. Senthil Kumar.

pressHints.headline: Tollywood's Costliest ~₹40 Cr Bet on a 2nd-Film Hero
pressHints.body: Backed by Allu Aravind's Geetha Arts, trade pandits were stunned by its unprecedented 2009 budget for a lead star appearing in only his second movie.

pressHints.headline: A Classic 90s Remix & Surprise Megastar Cameo
pressHints.body: S.S. Rajamouli & M.M. Keeravani sent theatres into total madness with a surprise Chiranjeevi cameo during a remixed chartbuster alongside Ram Charan and Kajal Aggarwal.

pressHints.headline: 100 Soldiers vs 1 Warrior & 'Send Them All At Once!'
pressHints.body: Immortalized by Peter Hein's horseback sword-fighting choreography, Srihari's 'Sher Khan' challenge, and 400-year electric-touch romance.

title: Maryada Ramanna
tropes: Rayalaseema faction village backdrop with a generations-old blood feud
Innocent, timid delivery guy Ramu visits ancestral village to sell land
Rival faction family follows strict hospitality rules and cannot kill him while inside their house
Hilarious cat-and-mouse survival comedy inside a factionist mansion
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Features a talking bicycle voiced by Ravi Teja and a thrilling railway track chase
iconicProp: A talking bicycle voiced by Ravi Teja
hint: As long as he doesn't step outside the factionist's front gate, he's completely safe.
eraTrivia: Released July 23, 2010 right after Rajamouli's giant industry hit—surprising everyone by casting a top comedian as the solo hero!
Inspired loosely by Buster Keaton's 1923 silent classic 'Our Hospitality'
Won 4 Nandi Awards including Best Popular Feature Film and Best Villain (Nagineedu)
Remade across India—including Hindi ('Son of Sardaar' starring Ajay Devgn), Tamil ('Vallavanukku Pullum Aayudham'), Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali
Produced by Arka Media Works (the same producers who later backed Baahubali!)
iconicMoments: Mass Maharaja Ravi Teja lending his hilarious voice to a sarcastic old bicycle
Nail-biting yet laugh-out-loud survival tricks inside a Rayalaseema faction house
High-energy songs like 'Ammayi Kitiki Pakkana' and 'Telugammayi'

pressHints.headline: Inspired by a 1923 Buster Keaton Silent Comedy Classic
pressHints.body: Produced by Arka Media Works before their pan-India epics, this clever 2010 caper won 4 Nandi Awards and adapted a 1923 silent-era hospitality premise for Telugu audiences.

pressHints.headline: Remade in Hindi as 'Son of Sardaar' & Across 4 Other Languages
pressHints.body: Its hilarious high-concept premise became an instant remake magnet across Bollywood, Kollywood, Sandalwood, Mollywood, and Bengali cinema.

pressHints.headline: Right After an Industry Hit, the Director Cast a Comedian as Solo Hero
pressHints.body: In July 2010, fans were stunned when Tollywood's biggest blockbuster director followed up an epic hit with a tight comedy-thriller starring a beloved comedian as the lead!

pressHints.headline: Rajamouli + Keeravani + Ravi Teja's Hilarious Voiceover
pressHints.body: Directed by S.S. Rajamouli with music by M.M. Keeravani, starring Sunil opposite Saloni Aswani and Nagineedu—with Ravi Teja voicing an inanimate prop!

pressHints.headline: A Talking Bicycle & Rayalaseema 'Atithi Devo Bhava' Hospitality
pressHints.body: Best remembered for a sarcastic talking bicycle and a factionist household that cannot touch their guest as long as he refuses to cross the front doorstep!

title: Khaleja
tropes: Witty, sarcastic Hyderabad taxi driver Seetharama Raju is worshipped as God by desperate villagers
Remote Pali village suffers from a mysterious plague caused by illegal corporate mining
Hilarious Rajasthan desert road trip with perpetually unlucky heroine Subhashini
Features Brahmanandam as Miriyam, the quirky sidekick of villain GK (Prakash Raj)
Sharp Trivikram comedy punchlines mixed with mythic heroism
Sada Siva Sanyasi devotional-action elevation sequence
iconicProp: Yellow-and-black Hyderabad taxi cab & ancient village prophecy scroll
hint: A sarcastic cab driver insists he's just a human while an entire poisoned village insists he's God.
eraTrivia: Released October 7, 2010 marking Mahesh Babu's return to the big screen after a 3-year hiatus—initially underperformed in theatres before becoming one of Tollywood's most fiercely loved cult classics!
Ramajogayya Sastry won the Filmfare Award South for Best Lyricist for the thunderous 'Sada Siva Sanyasi'
Shot extensively across blistering Rajasthan deserts and Hyderabad
Now celebrated by Telugu cinema fans as having the sharpest comedy timing of Mahesh Babu's entire career
Marked the second collaboration between Mahesh Babu and Trivikram Srinivas
iconicMoments: Electrifying 'Sada Siva Sanyasi' interval elevation in a swirling sandstorm
Non-stop sarcastic cab-driver banter with Anushka and Sunil across Rajasthan
Brahmanandam as 'Miriyam' and Prakash Raj's corporate villain monologues

pressHints.headline: Underperformed in Oct 2010, Then Became an Obsessive Cult Classic
pressHints.body: Marked a superstar's comeback after a 3-year break from theatres—initially divided 2010 box-office pundits, yet grew into one of Telugu social media's most re-watched comedy gems.

pressHints.headline: Won Filmfare Best Lyricist for a Roaring Devotional-Action Anthem
pressHints.body: Ramajogayya Sastry and Mani Sharma created a spine-tingling Shiva anthem that became one of the most iconic interval elevations of the 2010s.

pressHints.headline: Blistering Rajasthan Road Trip + Peak Sarcastic One-Liners
pressHints.body: Fans still crown this film as the lead star's all-time peak comic timing—backed by Sunil, Ali, Rao Ramesh, and Brahmanandam as 'Miriyam'.

pressHints.headline: Mahesh Babu + Trivikram Reunion With Anushka & Prakash Raj
pressHints.body: The second collaboration between Mahesh Babu and Trivikram Srinivas, pairing him with Anushka Shetty against corporate mining mogul Prakash Raj.

pressHints.headline: A Sarcastic Hyderabad Taxi Driver Worshipped as God
pressHints.body: Unforgettable for its yellow-black taxi cab, 'Sada Siva Sanyasi' sandstorm sequence, and a baffled cabbie insisting he's just an ordinary guy!

title: Eega
tropes: Murdered young lover reincarnates as a tiny housefly to avenge his death
Obsessive billionaire industrialist Sudeep is terrorized by the relentless fly
Micro-artist heroine Bindu crafts miniature armor, masks, and weapons for the fly
Hilarious fly gym training montage lifting tiny weights
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Explosive climax using a miniature cannon and fireworks
iconicProp: Miniature fly-sized safety goggles & tiny needle sword
hint: The smallest action hero in Indian cinema history refuses to let a billionaire sleep.
eraTrivia: Released July 6, 2012 in Telugu & Tamil ('Naan Ee') and dubbed in Hindi as 'Makkhi'
Won 2 National Film Awards (Best Telugu Feature Film & Best Special Effects) and 9 awards at Toronto After Dark
Screened at the Cannes Film Market and Shanghai International Film Festival
Featured over 2,200 CGI shots by Makuta VFX; Kiccha Sudeep acted against laser pointers for half the film
iconicMoments: Hilarious tiny-weight gym workout montage with heroic background score
Micro-art goggles, mask, and miniature weapons crafted for a tiny hero
'I Will Kill You' scribble on a foggy bathroom mirror

pressHints.headline: Swept 9 Awards at Toronto After Dark & Screened at Cannes
pressHints.body: Became one of the rarest Telugu commercial films of the 2010s to tour global genre festivals—winning Most Original Film and Best Special Effects abroad.

pressHints.headline: 2 National Film Awards & Over 2,200 Makuta VFX Shots
pressHints.body: Backed by producer Sai Korrapati (Vaaraahi Chalana Chitram), it won the 60th National Film Awards for Best Telugu Film and Best Special Effects.

pressHints.headline: A Kannada Superstar Acted Against Thin Air & Stole the Show
pressHints.body: Released in July 2012 simultaneously in Telugu and Tamil; critics nationwide raved about the billionaire villain acting solo against laser pointers.

pressHints.headline: Rajamouli + Keeravani Pairing Nani & Samantha
pressHints.body: Helmed by S.S. Rajamouli with music by M.M. Keeravani and cinematography by K.K. Senthil Kumar, featuring Natural Star Nani opposite Samantha Ruth Prabhu.

pressHints.headline: Miniature Safety Goggles, Micro-Art & A Tiny Gym Montage
pressHints.body: Unforgettable for its hilarious tiny-weight gym workout montage, micro-art miniature weapons, and the smallest revenge hero in Indian cinema!

title: Baahubali: The Beginning
tropes: Orphan Shivudu raised in a tribal village near a towering waterfall climbs the cliff
Carries a massive stone Shiva Lingam on his shoulder under the waterfall
Ancient kingdom of Mahishmati ruled by ruthless king Bhallaladeva (Rana Daggubati)
Epic war against the Kalakeya tribe using the Trishul battle formation
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Iconic pan-India cliffhanger: 'Why did Kattappa kill Baahubali?'
iconicProp: Wooden warrior mask & giant Shiva Lingam
hint: He climbed an impossible waterfall and left all of India asking one question for two years.
eraTrivia: Released July 10, 2015 and became the first Telugu film to win the National Film Award for Best Feature Film (Golden Lotus)
Invented an entirely new 750-word fictional tribal language called 'Kiliki' created by lyricist Madhan Karky
Grossed over 600+ crore worldwide—launching the modern Pan-India cinema era from Hyderabad
Shot at Athirappilly Falls (Kerala), Bulgaria, Mahabaleshwar, and giant Sabu Cyril sets at Ramoji Film City
Its cliffhanger ending sparked India's biggest pop-culture meme question for nearly two full years
iconicMoments: Lifting a giant stone Shiva Lingam on his shoulder beneath towering waterfalls
The grand Trishul war formation battle with flaming wheels and chariot blades
Rajamatha Sivagami holding an infant above raging floodwaters

pressHints.headline: Commissioned a Brand-New 750-Word Fictional Language ('Kiliki')
pressHints.body: Lyricist Madhan Karky invented an entire 750-word phonetic language with 40 grammar rules specifically for the rival warlord tribe in this 2015 spectacle.

pressHints.headline: First Telugu Film Ever to Win National Best Feature Film
pressHints.body: Released in July 2015 under Arka Media Works, it took home the Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus) for Best Feature Film and Best Special Effects.

pressHints.headline: Smashed ₹600+ Cr Worldwide & Birthed the Pan-India Era
pressHints.body: Shot at Athirappilly Falls and colossal Sabu Cyril palace sets at Ramoji Film City, it proved a Telugu film could shatter Hindi and global box-office records.

pressHints.headline: Prabhas + Rana + Ramya Krishna + Sathyaraj + Rajamouli
pressHints.body: Directed by S.S. Rajamouli with music by M.M. Keeravani, starring Prabhas, Rana Daggubati, Tamannaah, Anushka Shetty, and a cameo by Kiccha Sudeep.

pressHints.headline: Giant Waterfall Shiva Lingam & India's Biggest 2-Year Question
pressHints.body: Left the entire country obsessed for two years with one immortal meme question involving loyal warrior Kattappa!

title: Pelli Choopulu
tropes: Aimless engineering graduate Prashanth meets fiercely ambitious Chitra during an arranged-marriage matchmaking mix-up
They get accidentally locked in a room together and share their life stories
Launch a quirky food truck business ('Spitfire') together in Hyderabad
Features Priyadarshi's breakout Telangana comedy role ('Naa saavu nenu sastha, neekenduku!')
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Breezy indie-style Hyderabadi rom-com that changed new-age Telugu cinema
hint: A matchmaking mix-up locks two strangers in a room—and sparks Hyderabad's cutest food truck startup.
eraTrivia: Made on a tiny indie budget of around 1.25 crore in July 2016 and grossed over 30+ crore—becoming a watershed hit for new-wave Telugu cinema
Won 2 National Film Awards at the 64th National Film Awards: Best Telugu Feature Film and Best Dialogues (Tharun Bhascker)
S.S. Rajamouli famously praised the film on social media during opening week, triggering massive word-of-mouth
Launched the breakthrough careers of Vijay Deverakonda, Tharun Bhascker, Priyadarshi, and indie composer Vivek Sagar
Remade in Hindi as 'Mitron' (2018) and in Malayalam as 'Vijay Superum Pournamiyum'
iconicMoments: Priyadarshi's legendary Telangana comic outburst: 'Naa saavu nenu sastha, neekenduku!'
Breezy rooftop conversations and indie guitar soundtrack ('Merise Merise', 'Chinuku Taake')
The charming yellow food-truck startup hustle around Hyderabad

pressHints.headline: Made on ~₹1.25 Crore & Won 2 National Film Awards
pressHints.body: Sparked Telugu cinema's modern indie new-wave in July 2016—earning over 20x its tiny budget and winning National Awards for Best Telugu Film and Best Dialogues.

pressHints.headline: An Endorsement From S.S. Rajamouli Ignited Word-of-Mouth
pressHints.body: Opened with minimal buzz until S.S. Rajamouli praised its fresh writing online—soon getting remade in Hindi ('Mitron') and Malayalam.

pressHints.headline: Gave Birth to Priyadarshi's Immortal 'Naa Saavu Nenu Sastha!' Meme
pressHints.body: Made overnight stars out of Telangana-slang comedian Priyadarshi and fresh indie music composer Vivek Sagar ('Merise Merise').

pressHints.headline: Tharun Bhascker's Debut Starring Vijay Deverakonda & Ritu Varma
pressHints.body: Written and directed by short-film alumnus Tharun Bhascker, putting Vijay Deverakonda in his first solo blockbuster opposite Ritu Varma.

pressHints.headline: An Arranged-Marriage Mix-Up & A Yellow Food Truck Startup
pressHints.body: Beloved for locking two complete opposites in a room during a matchmaking visit—and turning them into Hyderabad's coolest food-truck co-founders!

title: Arjun Reddy
tropes: Brilliant orthopedic house surgeon with severe anger management issues
Intense senior-junior medical college romance in Mangalore with Preeti
Family opposition separates the lovers, triggering a spiral of alcohol and heartbreak
Loyal best friend Shiva (Rahul Ramakrishna) stands by him through chaos
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Urban character study with raw dialogues, Royal Enfield bike, and medical board trial
iconicProp: Royal Enfield Bullet & a surgeon's stethoscope
hint: A short-tempered medical topper spirals into chaos after losing his college sweetheart.
eraTrivia: Released August 25, 2017 after a fiery Censor Board 'A' certification battle and poster controversy in Hyderabad
Made on roughly 5 crore (funded partly by selling family land!) and grossed over 50+ crore—turning into a cultural earthquake
Remade in Hindi by the same director as the blockbuster 'Kabir Singh' (2019) and in Tamil as 'Adithya Varma'
Vijay Deverakonda famously auctioned his Filmfare Best Actor trophy for 25 lakh for the CM Relief Fund
Launched Rahul Ramakrishna as one of Telugu cinema's most popular character actors
iconicMoments: Raw, unfiltered Telangana-English college banter with loyal sidekick Shiva
Iconic messy-beard look, Royal Enfield Bullet roar, and Harshavardhan Rameshwar's haunting BGM
Heart-wrenching acoustic soundtrack ('Emitemitemo', 'Telisiney Na Nuvvey')

pressHints.headline: Funded With Family Savings & Sparked a Fiery Censor Poster Row
pressHints.body: Released in late August 2017 on a ~₹5 crore budget after intense debates over its bold posters and 'A' certificate—then stormed past ₹50 crore!

pressHints.headline: Its Lead Star Auctioned His Filmfare Trophy for ₹25 Lakh
pressHints.body: Generated massive headlines when the lead actor won Filmfare Best Actor and auctioned the physical trophy for charity—while Rahul Ramakrishna became an instant fan favorite.

pressHints.headline: Its Debut Director Remade It in Hindi as 'Kabir Singh'
pressHints.body: Two years later, the exact same writer-director helmed its mega-blockbuster Bollywood remake (and a Tamil version also followed).

pressHints.headline: Sandeep Reddy Vanga + Vijay Deverakonda + Shalini Pandey
pressHints.body: Featured Radhan's soulful songs ('Emitemitemo') and Harshavardhan Rameshwar's unforgettable theme score, shot in Mangalore and Hyderabad.

pressHints.headline: Royal Enfield Bullet, Stethoscope & A Short-Tempered Surgeon
pressHints.body: Defined 2017 youth fashion with its messy beard, sunglasses, medical-college romance, and raw emotional intensity.

title: Rangasthalam
tropes: 1980s Godavari rural village backdrop drenched in rustic local politics
Partially deaf hero Chitti Babu operates a diesel water pump motor for farms
Ruthless village President Phanindra Bhupathi (Jagapathi Babu) rules unopposed for 30 years
Elder brother Kumar Babu (Aadhi Pinisetty) returns from Dubai to challenge the President in village elections
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Shocking final-act political betrayal twist involving MLA Dakshina Murthy (Prakash Raj)
iconicProp: Diesel farm water pump motor & a checkered lungi
hint: A hearing-impaired 1980s village sound engineer takes on a tyrannical village president.
eraTrivia: Released March 30, 2018 and crossed 200+ crore worldwide as the highest-grossing non-Baahubali Telugu film of its time
Won the 66th National Film Award for Best Audiography (Sound Mixing)
Built an entire 1980s Godavari village set from scratch on a 20-acre plot near Hyderabad
Entire album written by Chandrabose and composed by DSP, featuring Pooja Hegde in 'Jigelu Rani'
iconicMoments: Raw bearded lungi transformation with thick Godavari dialect
Hand-cranked diesel water motor scenes and Ram-Lakshman's dusty village stunts
Viral retro-bulb special song 'Jigelu Rani' and Anasuya's breakout 'Rangammatta'

pressHints.headline: Honored Nationally for Sound Craft & Vintage Lenses
pressHints.body: Shot with vintage anamorphic lenses by R. Rathnavelu, this film won a National Film Award strictly for Best Audiography (Sound Mixing).

pressHints.headline: An Entire Retro Rural Settlement Built on 20 Acres
pressHints.body: Art directors constructed a hyper-detailed 1980s village from scratch on a 20-acre plot near Hyderabad under Mythri Movie Makers.

pressHints.headline: Late March 2018 Word-of-Mouth & Breakout Supporting Star
pressHints.body: Hit theatres in late March 2018 to roaring reviews—also famous for a fierce rustic breakout turn by popular TV anchor-turned-actress Anasuya.

pressHints.headline: DSP–Chandrabose Album & ₹200+ Crore Non-Baahubali Record
pressHints.body: Every song was penned by Chandrabose and scored by Devi Sri Prasad—propelling Sukumar's film past ₹200 crore worldwide.

pressHints.headline: Bearded Lungi Swagger, Godavari Slang & 'Jigelu Rani'
pressHints.body: Celebrated for Ram Charan's raw lungi makeover opposite Samantha, diesel farm motor sounds, and Pooja Hegde's viral retro special song!

title: Jersey
tropes: 36-year-old failed Ranji cricketer Arjun returns to cricket to buy his young son a team jersey
Set across 1986 and 1996 Hyderabad domestic cricket circuits
Emotional railway-station screaming catharsis scene that became legendary
Supportive coach Murthy (Sathyaraj) believes in his late comeback
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Poignant final-act twist honoring a father's quiet sacrifice
iconicProp: ₹500 Indian cricket jersey & a battered wooden cricket bat
hint: A 36-year-old father steps back onto the pitch to prove it's never too late to be his son's hero.
eraTrivia: Released April 19, 2019 under Sithara Entertainments and won 2 National Film Awards: Best Telugu Feature Film and Best Editing (Naveen Nooli)
Anirudh Ravichander's rousing 'Spirit of Jersey' background score became one of Indian cinema's most iconic motivational themes
Nani trained rigorously with real cricketers and even suffered a real nose injury on set during practice!
Remade in Hindi in 2022 by the same director Gowtam Tinnanuri starring Shahid Kapoor
Named one of the greatest Indian sports dramas of the decade by critics and fans alike
iconicMoments: The goosebumps-inducing railway-station scream as a train rushes past
Anirudh's soaring 'Spirit of Jersey' and 'Adhento Gaani Vunnapaatuga' melodies
Father-son warmth set against crisp 1990s Hyderabad Ranji cricket grounds

pressHints.headline: Won 2 National Film Awards Including Best Editing (Naveen Nooli)
pressHints.body: Backed by Sithara Entertainments in April 2019, this emotional drama took home National Awards for Best Telugu Feature Film and Best Editing.

pressHints.headline: The Hero Broke His Nose Training + Got a 2022 Hindi Remake
pressHints.body: The lead star trained like a pro athlete—even suffering a real facial injury during shoots—before its own director remade it in Hindi with Shahid Kapoor.

pressHints.headline: Anirudh Ravichander's Soaring Motivational Theme Broke the Internet
pressHints.body: Rockstar composer Anirudh delivered a career-best emotional soundtrack and goosebumps theme score alongside Sanu Varghese's nostalgic 1990s visuals.

pressHints.headline: Gowtam Tinnanuri + Nani + Shraddha Srinath + Sathyaraj
pressHints.body: Directed by Gowtam Tinnanuri, starring Natural Star Nani in a career-defining performance opposite Shraddha Srinath with Sathyaraj as his mentor.

pressHints.headline: The Railway Station Scream & A 36-Year-Old Cricketer's Comeback
pressHints.body: Immortalized by an emotional train-station roar and a father stepping back onto the Ranji cricket pitch for his little boy's birthday wish!

title: Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo
tropes: Two newborn babies are secretly swapped at a hospital by envious clerk Valmiki (Murali Sharma)
Witty middle-class Bantu discovers he is actually the biological heir to a billionaire mansion
Corporate office romance with stylish boss Amulya
Chartbuster songs 'Butta Bomma', 'Samajavaragamana', and 'Ramuloo Ramulaa'
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Iconic boardroom musical showdown and stylish slow-motion coat fight at the shipyard
iconicProp: Swapped hospital crib tag & a sharp designer boardroom suit
hint: Swapped at birth by a jealous clerk, he dances his way straight into his real billionaire home.
eraTrivia: Released January 12, 2020 for Sankranthi and became one of the highest-grossing Telugu films ever (260+ crore worldwide)
Thaman S won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction—with 'Butta Bomma' crossing 850M+ YouTube views and even going viral with Australian cricketer David Warner!
Marked veteran actress Tabu's celebrated return to Telugu cinema after over a decade
Remade in Hindi as 'Shehzada' (2023) starring Kartik Aaryan
Marked the hat-trick collaboration between Allu Arjun and Trivikram Srinivas
iconicMoments: The viral 'Butta Bomma' dance hook and 'Samajavaragamana' Eiffel Tower visuals
An iconic boardroom musical medley showdown confronting a stunned corporate board
Stylish slow-motion coat-adjusting shipyard action set to classic 'Sitharala Sirapadu'

pressHints.headline: Won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction
pressHints.body: Shot stylishly by P.S. Vinod and edited by Naveen Nooli, its chart-shattering 2020 album earned its composer his very first National Film Award!

pressHints.headline: Even Australian Cricketer David Warner Danced to Its Viral Song!
pressHints.body: Released for Sankranthi 2020 right before lockdowns, its songs crossed a billion+ combined streams and triggered global TikTok/Reels dance crazes.

pressHints.headline: Marked Tabu's Telugu Comeback & Got a 2023 Hindi Remake
pressHints.body: Grossed ₹260+ crore worldwide under Geetha Arts & Haarika Hassine—featuring Murali Sharma, Jayaram, Tabu, Sunil, and Vennela Kishore.

pressHints.headline: Allu Arjun + Trivikram Hat-Trick With Pooja Hegde & Thaman
pressHints.body: Reunited Allu Arjun and Trivikram Srinivas for the third time with Pooja Hegde as his chic corporate boss and Thaman S on music.

pressHints.headline: 'Butta Bomma', 'Samajavaragamana' & The Boardroom Medley
pressHints.body: Unforgettable for its hospital baby-swap premise, boardroom retro-song showdown, and sleek shipyard coat-fight swagger!

title: Pushpa: The Rise
tropes: 1990s Seshachalam forest and rural Chittoor backdrop centered on red sandalwood smuggling
Daily-wage coolie Pushpa Raj rises aggressively to become boss of the entire syndicate
Iconic crooked shoulder walk and chin-sweep 'Thaggede Le' attitude
Deep personal struggle as an illegitimate son denied his father's family surname
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Pan-India mass blockbuster with viral songs 'Srivalli' and 'Oo Antava' and cop rival Shekhawat (Fahadh Faasil)
iconicProp: Smuggled red sandalwood log & a forest axe
hint: Flower anukunnava? Fire! A red sandalwood coolie refuses to bow down to anyone.
eraTrivia: Released December 17, 2021 and became India's highest-grossing film of 2021 (~365+ crore), exploding unexpectedly in Hindi single-screen theatres
Made history at the 69th National Film Awards: Allu Arjun became the VERY FIRST Telugu actor ever to win Best Actor, and DSP won Best Music Direction!
Marked Malayalam star Fahadh Faasil's electrifying Telugu cinema debut
Filmed in dense Maredumilli forests with Polish cinematographer Miroslaw Kuba Brozek
Spawned global cricketing & pop-culture fever around the 'Srivalli' slipper-drop walk and chin-sweep gesture
iconicMoments: Crooked shoulder walk and iconic chin-brush 'Thaggede Le!' swagger
Samantha Ruth Prabhu's sensation 'Oo Antava' and the 'Srivalli' slipper-drop hook step
Tense final-act psychological face-off against a quirky bald IPS officer

pressHints.headline: Shot in Maredumilli Forests by a Polish Cinematographer
pressHints.body: Produced by Mythri Movie Makers in late 2021, this gritty crime drama brought in Polish DOP Miroslaw Kuba Brozek and marked a celebrated Malayalam star's Telugu debut.

pressHints.headline: First Telugu Actor in History to Win National Best Actor!
pressHints.body: Created Indian cinema history at the 69th National Film Awards by winning Telugu cinema's very first Best Actor trophy alongside Best Music Direction.

pressHints.headline: Exploded in Hindi Single Screens to Top 2021's Box Office
pressHints.body: Became India's highest-grossing movie of 2021—with Sunil & Anasuya shocking fans in menacing villain avatars and Samantha blazing in a viral special song.

pressHints.headline: Sukumar + Allu Arjun + Rashmika + Fahadh Faasil + DSP
pressHints.body: Reunited Sukumar, Allu Arjun, and Devi Sri Prasad alongside Rashmika Mandanna and Fahadh Faasil in a Chittoor forest smuggling empire.

pressHints.headline: 'Thaggede Le!', Red Sandalwood & The 'Srivalli' Slipper Walk
pressHints.body: Worldwide pop-culture madness over 'Flower anukunnava? Fire!', a crooked shoulder swagger, and the 'Oo Antava' chartbuster!

title: RRR
hero: N.T. Rama Rao Jr. & Ram Charan
tropes: 1920s British Colonial India fictional bromance between Alluri Sitarama Raju and Komaram Bheem
Fire and Water symbolism—two revolutionaries rescue a boy together on a burning railway bridge
Wild tigers, leopards, and deer leap out of a truck at the British Governor's palace party
Oscar-winning global chartbuster dance battle 'Naatu Naatu'
Does not feature Brahmanandam
Pan-India period action epic about rescuing a kidnapped Gond tribal girl named Malli
iconicProp: Flaming bow & arrows and British suspenders from Naatu Naatu
hint: Fire meets water in 1920s India, culminating in an Oscar-winning dance showdown.
eraTrivia: Released March 25, 2022 and grossed over 1,200+ crore worldwide—also breaking Japanese box-office records for Indian cinema!
Made global history by winning the Academy Award (Oscar) and Golden Globe for Best Original Song ('Naatu Naatu' by M.M. Keeravani & Chandrabose)
Swept 6 National Film Awards (including Best Popular Film, Best Music BGM, Best Choreography, Best Action, Best VFX)
Famously filmed its iconic dance sequence right in front of Ukraine's Mariinskyi Presidential Palace in Kyiv in 2021!
Praised publicly by Hollywood legends James Cameron and Steven Spielberg
iconicMoments: Wild tigers and leopards leaping out of a truck in slow-motion at a British palace party
The jaw-dropping Fire & Water bridge rescue of a boy using a horse, motorcycle, and flag
The electrifying synchronized suspender dance battle 'Naatu Naatu'

pressHints.headline: Shot a Legendary Sequence at Ukraine's Presidential Palace + Broke Japan Records
pressHints.body: Filmed in Kyiv months before global headlines, produced by D.V.V. Danayya, and praised personally by Hollywood legends James Cameron and Steven Spielberg.

pressHints.headline: Swept 6 National Awards & Grossed ₹1,200+ Crore Worldwide
pressHints.body: Released in March 2022 after pandemic delays, winning National Awards across Choreography, Action Stunts, VFX, BGM, and Best Popular Film.

pressHints.headline: Two Telugu Mega-Stars + Alia Bhatt + Ajay Devgn + Ray Stevenson
pressHints.body: Brought Jr. NTR and Ram Charan together on screen for the first time in a roaring 1920s colonial-era bromance under S.S. Rajamouli.

pressHints.headline: Won Both the Oscar & Golden Globe for Best Original Song!
pressHints.body: M.M. Keeravani and Chandrabose brought home India's first feature-film Original Song Oscar, choreographed by Prem Rakshith.

pressHints.headline: Fire & Water Bridge Rescue, Palace Tigers & 'Naatu Naatu'
pressHints.body: Unforgettable for wild animals bursting out of a truck and two best friends dancing the British off the floor in synchronized suspenders!

title: Kalki 2898 AD
tropes: Dystopian futuristic Kasi in the year 2898 AD beneath a floating inverted pyramid called the Complex
Bounty hunter Bhairava (Prabhas) dreams of earning enough units to enter the Complex with his AI car Bujji
Immortal Mahabharata warrior Ashwatthama (Amitabh Bachchan) protects a pregnant fugitive (Deepika Padukone)
Supreme Yaskin (Kamal Haasan) rules the Complex seeking serum for eternal power
Features Brahmanandam as Rajan, Bhairava's hilarious futuristic landlord
Packed with surprise cameos by S.S. Rajamouli, Vijay Deverakonda, Dulquer Salmaan, Mrunal Thakur, and Ram Gopal Varma
iconicProp: Talking futuristic AI vehicle 'Bujji' & Ashwatthama's glowing forehead gem
hint: In dystopian Kasi 2898 AD, a bounty hunter with a sassy AI car clashes with an immortal Mahabharata warrior.
eraTrivia: Released June 27, 2024 as Indian cinema's most expensive sci-fi epic (~600 crore) under Vyjayanthi Movies, grossing over 1,040+ crore worldwide
Made history in July 2023 as the VERY FIRST Indian movie to launch its title teaser at San Diego Comic-Con (Hall H) under its working title 'Project K'!
Engineered a real 6-ton custom futuristic electric car ('Bujji') built with Mahindra & Jayem Automotives—voiced by National Award winner Keerthy Suresh!
Packed with viral surprise cameos by S.S. Rajamouli, Ram Gopal Varma, Vijay Deverakonda, Dulquer Salmaan, and Mrunal Thakur—plus Brahmanandam as a futuristic landlord!
Santhosh Narayanan blended mythological Sanskrit chants with cyberpunk synth scores
iconicMoments: A real-life futuristic 3-wheeled talking AI car ('Bujji') cracking jokes during high-speed chases
Amitabh Bachchan's towering, thunderous clash with Prabhas inside futuristic ruins
A jaw-dropping mythological climax reveal linking Mahabharata legends to the year 2898 AD

pressHints.headline: First Indian Film Ever to Launch in Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con
pressHints.body: Teased worldwide under the code name 'Project K' in 2023 before its June 2024 release—backed by Vyjayanthi Movies with Serbian DOP Djordje Stojiljkovic.

pressHints.headline: Built a Real 6-Ton Futuristic Electric Car With Mahindra!
pressHints.body: Its viral promotional tour showcased a custom-engineered 6-ton sci-fi vehicle driven across India—with Keerthy Suresh voicing its sassy AI personality.

pressHints.headline: ₹1,040+ Cr Blockbuster Packed With Shocking Director & Star Cameos
pressHints.body: Broke the ₹1,000 crore global barrier in 2024—featuring surprise cameos by S.S. Rajamouli, RGV, Vijay Deverakonda, Dulquer Salmaan, Mrunal Thakur, and Brahmanandam!

pressHints.headline: Nag Ashwin + Prabhas + Amitabh Bachchan + Kamal Haasan + Deepika
pressHints.body: Directed by Nag Ashwin with cyberpunk-mythological music by Santhosh Narayanan, uniting four generations of Indian cinema titans on one screen.

pressHints.headline: Dystopian Kasi, The Floating Complex & AI Sidekick 'Bujji'
pressHints.body: Blends Mahabharata mythology with 29th-century sci-fi as bounty hunter Bhairava collides with immortal warrior Ashwatthama!
